evals.prompt: Quick critique: I want to submit ten identical iPhone habit trackers, one per color theme, under separate Bundle IDs. Each has the same flow and features. I think the colors make them original. Do not browse or submit anything; assess this pitch with policy evidence explicitly unverified.
evals.expected_output: A quick product critique with an explicit originality risk gate, a substantive redesign, and clearly bounded policy evidence.
expectations: Identifies separate Bundle IDs for identical theme variants as a serious self-duplication risk and does not let a numeric score override it.
Suggests consolidating themes into one useful product rather than cosmetic changes or review evasion.
Reports originality risk even in Quick mode, while labeling current Apple policy and competitor evidence unverified.
Does not claim certain rejection or approval, browse against the request, or submit an app.

evals.prompt: Evaluate an iPhone couples widget that promises an always-live shared mood display and a recurring subscription. We only have mockups; no partner interviews, working sync, platform feasibility checks or competitor research. Give a concept-only critique without browsing, coding or changing the product yet.
evals.expected_output: A bounded critique of two-person activation, repeat value, widget feasibility, originality uncertainty and the smallest validation experiment.
expectations: Questions widget update and background assumptions without claiming arbitrary continuous updates are supported.
Examines both partners activation, consent, privacy, and subscription value rather than inferring demand from mockups.
Keeps originality and current platform evidence explicitly unresolved and avoids an unconditional build or submission recommendation.
Proposes a small test with observable success and failure conditions without implementing or contacting users.
